- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds a per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 routed-MoE path to Megatron inference for squared-ReLU (Nemotron-family) and SwiGLU experts, running on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs. It is CUDA-graph capturable and batch invariant, and comes with the same test coverage the torch MXFP8 path has: a bitwise quantizer reference, a BF16 accuracy check, CUDA-graph replay, batch invariance, and a train-gen parity test against TE NVFP4 training. The NVFP4 weight path, CUDA-graph-stable refresh, batch-invariant finalize and tests are shared by FlashInfer's other NVFP4-weight recipes (per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 and BF16 x NVFP4), so adding those later only changes the activation side; see "Strength: one integration for every NVFP4-weight recipe" and "How to extend".

## Background

**Recipe.** Weights are NVFP4 with 1x16 E4M3 block scales and one FP32 global scale per expert. Activations are quantized online with one FP32 scale per token instead of a static, calibrated per-tensor input scale. That removes the calibration step and the activation-outlier sensitivity of a per-tensor scale, which matters in RL because the policy weights change every step.

**Kernel level (FlashInfer).** All kernels already exist upstream; this PR only integrates them.
- [flashinfer#3027](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3027) adds per-token NVFP4 quantization (`nvfp4_quantize(..., per_token_activation=True)`) and the per-token TRT-LLM-gen MoE.
- [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645) adds per-token NVFP4 activations to the CuTe DSL MoE (`CuteDslMoEWrapper.run(..., per_token_scale=...)`), the backend this PR uses.
- [flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976) adds the deterministic two-stage finalize (`use_fused_finalize=False`) to the CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE, which batch-invariant mode uses.
- [flashinfer#4618](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4618) adds the ReLU2 (squared-ReLU) activation for per-token NVFP4 MoE, which Nemotron needs.
- FlashInfer 0.7.0 ships per-token NVFP4 with ReLU2 and SwiGLU on both the TRT-LLM-gen and the CuTe DSL (`CuteDslMoEWrapper`, `quant_mode="w4a4"`) MoE backends.

**Engine level (peers of Megatron inference).**
- [sglang#22918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22918) adds `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION`, which replaces the checkpoint's static input scales with 1 so FlashInfer computes per-token scales at runtime.
- [sglang#39199](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39199) routes ReLU2 per-token NVFP4 MoE to TRT-LLM-gen, padding hidden to 512 and intermediate to 128.
- Both are validated with GSM8K accuracy thresholds. Neither tests bitwise behavior, batch invariance, CUDA graphs, or train-gen parity.

**RL level.**
- [NeMo-RL#3566](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/3566) trains with TE NVFP4 (per-token activation scaling on routed experts), refits BF16 weights into vLLM, and quantizes the routed-expert weights to NVFP4 inside the rollout worker.
- [miles#1261](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/1261) does NVFP4 rollout/train with TE's `NVFP4Quantizer` producing the checkpoint and SGLang (FlashInfer TRT-LLM routed MoE) serving it.
- Both keep BF16 as the refit format and quantize on the inference side. This PR brings the same design to Megatron inference, so Megatron RL can roll out in per-token NVFP4 without an external engine.

**What Transformer Engine already has.** TE's `NVFP4BlockScaling` recipe supports `row_scaled_activation=True` (one scale per token), and with `disable_2d_quantization=True`, `disable_rht=True` and `disable_stochastic_rounding=True` it is the training-side form of this recipe. That is what NeMo-RL#3566 trains with, and it is the reference for the train-gen parity test below, in the same way TE MXFP8 is the reference for the MXFP8 inference path ([#8195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8195)). TE has no inference MoE kernel for this recipe, so inference uses FlashInfer.

## What is added

**New config field.** `inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe: Optional[Literal['per_token']] = None` in `TransformerConfig` (`--inference-moe-nvfp4-recipe per_token`). It is a recipe choice rather than a bool so the other NVFP4 recipes (see "How to extend") can be added as new values. It requires `transformer_impl='inference_optimized'`, `inference_grouped_gemm_backend='flashinfer'`, non-gated `squared_relu` experts or gated `F.silu` (SwiGLU, `gated_linear_unit=True`) experts, without `activation_func_tanh_clamp_scale` and, for SwiGLU, without `activation_func_clamp_value`, `glu_linear_offset` or `moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size`, BF16 expert parameters (no `fp8` / `fp4_param`), and FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 on SM100/SM103. Validation rejects every other combination with a specific error. `batch_invariant_mode` is allowed with this recipe (with the NVLS dispatcher when EP > 1), as it is for FlashInfer MXFP8.

**`megatron/core/inference/moe/flashinfer_nvfp4.py` (new).**
- `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` quantizes the BF16 FC1/FC2 expert stacks into the CuTe DSL layout: packed E2M1, 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales plus their MMA view, and per-expert FP32 alphas. SwiGLU is detected from the shapes (FC1 has twice FC2's input width): MCore's `[gate; up]` FC1 is padded per half and reordered into FlashInfer's alternating 64-row `[up, gate]` blocks. With `out=` it refreshes the existing buffers in place, so addresses captured by CUDA graphs stay valid across refits.
- `quantize_routed_nvfp4_input` pads and quantizes activations per token. The global scale is the recipe constant `1 / (448 * 6)` passed as a Python float, so there is no host sync and it is graph-safe.
- `flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe` runs `CuteDslMoEWrapper`. Wrappers are cached per shape and created outside graph capture. Under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms` or batch-invariant mode it uses the two-stage finalize, which reduces each token's top-k routes in a fixed order, instead of the fused atomic finalize. With the NVLS dispatcher it writes straight into the reduce-scatter buffer, so `ordered_reduce_scatter_v` keeps the cross-rank reduction order fixed.

**`InferenceGroupedMLP` (`experts.py`).** The BF16 expert stacks stay resident as the canonical weights and refit destination. The NVFP4 copy is built on the first inference forward, and the FlashInfer forward dispatches to it. `refresh_flashinfer_nvfp4_weights()` requantizes it in place.

**Not in this PR: refit and RL.** Nothing calls `refresh_flashinfer_nvfp4_weights()` after a refit or an optimizer step yet, so don't set `inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe` for RL rollouts until the follow-up PR (TODO: link) lands. That PR wires the refresh into `megatron/core/resharding/refit.py` and `megatron/rl/rl_utils.py`; it is split out to keep the refit and RL reviewer groups off this PR. Static inference from a loaded checkpoint is unaffected.

**`moe_layer.py`.** The NVFP4 path checks for the FlashInfer per-token APIs instead of `flashinfer-jit-cache`, because CuTe DSL kernels are JIT-compiled through `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` rather than shipped in the jit-cache wheel.

**Dependencies.** `flashinfer-python` is relaxed from `<0.7.0` to `<0.8.0` and `uv.lock` moves to 0.7.0.post1, which adds `nccl-extensions`. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` is already a dependency of `flashinfer-python`.

### Why CuTe DSL and not TRT-LLM-gen

Both FlashInfer backends support per-token NVFP4 with ReLU2 and SwiGLU on SM100/SM103. An earlier revision of this PR supported both; we kept only CuTe DSL:
- **No runtime downloads.** TRT-LLM-gen loads its cubins from an artifactory at first use (into `~/.cache/flashinfer/cubins` unless `flashinfer-cubin` is installed). On our test node that download failed with "Disk quota exceeded" and the GEMM then failed at 128 and 256 tokens. CuTe DSL compiles locally through `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`.
- **Controllable determinism.** CuTe DSL exposes `use_fused_finalize` ([flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976)), which gives a fixed-order top-k reduction for batch-invariant mode. #3976 measures its cost at about 1.5-14% over the atomic finalize, highest at 1-4 tokens.
- **Less padding and simpler weight prep.** CuTe DSL pads to 256 (Nemotron 2688 -> 2816 hidden) where TRT-LLM-gen pads to 512 (2688 -> 3072), and it needs no TRT-LLM weight shuffling. A full requantization of 32 local experts (what each refit will cost) takes 16.7 ms against 21.5 ms for TRT-LLM-gen.
- **No speed reason to keep TRT-LLM-gen.** FlashInfer's own per-token comparison in [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645) (`bench_moe_deepseek.py --use-per-token-activation`, DeepSeek-V3 shapes, B200, CUDA graphs) has TRT-LLM-gen about 12% faster at 128-256 tokens and CuTe DSL 1.12-1.29x faster from 512 to 4096 tokens, a 1.08x geomean in CuTe DSL's favor. Our earlier Nemotron-shape runs on GB300 showed the same pattern.

One backend also halves the test matrix and removes a config field.

### Performance

MoE layer forward (router, dispatcher, experts and combine) under CUDA-graph replay, on one GB300 with EP = 1. The shapes are the DeepSeek-V3 shapes that FlashInfer uses for its per-token CuTe DSL vs TRT-LLM-gen comparison in [flashinfer#3645](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645): hidden 7168, intermediate 2048, 256 experts (all local) and top-8. There are two differences from #3645. The experts are squared-ReLU, Nemotron's activation, where #3645 uses SwiGLU. TODO: add the SwiGLU numbers (`bench_moe_layer.py --activation swiglu`). Routing is plain top-8 without group-limited routing, because Megatron's inference router does not support it. All three backends load the same BF16 weights. Times are in µs, the mean over 50 replays.

| Tokens | Default: vLLM BF16 | Default: torch MXFP8 | Default: NVFP4 (this PR) | Batch-inv.: vLLM BF16 | Batch-inv.: torch MXFP8 | Batch-inv.: NVFP4 (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 140.4 | 138.2 | **56.6** | 179.7 | 237.4 | **82.3** |
| 8 | 507.1 | 526.4 | **187.2** | 575.3 | 488.1 | **215.2** |
| 32 | 1389.8 | 1604.4 | **488.7** | 1502.3 | 1188.0 | **522.7** |
| 64 | 1878.8 | 2074.0 | **626.9** | 1990.7 | 1519.1 | **662.7** |
| 128 | 2162.9 | 2352.7 | **704.1** | 2216.6 | 1695.1 | **739.8** |
| 256 | 2247.1 | 2407.9 | **723.7** | 2339.4 | 1739.6 | **758.1** |
| 512 | 2336.9 | 2433.8 | **739.0** | 2498.8 | 1792.4 | **772.5** |
| 1024 | 2732.7 | 2486.9 | **767.4** | 2994.2 | 1889.0 | **810.5** |
| 2048 | 3003.8 | 2650.0 | **822.5** | 3502.6 | 2081.8 | **879.0** |
| 4096 | 4054.7 | 3474.3 | **1015.6** | 5006.8 | 2560.6 | **1107.4** |

Batch-invariant mode uses the `te_native` backend for the non-MoE GEMMs (router) in all three columns.

- **Default mode:** NVFP4 is 2.5x faster than BF16 at 1 token, 3.2x at 512 and 4.0x at 4096, and 3.2-3.4x faster than MXFP8 from 64 tokens up.
- **Batch-invariant mode:** NVFP4 is 2.2x faster than BF16 at 1 token, 3.2x at 512 and 4.5x at 4096, and about 2.3x faster than MXFP8 from 8 tokens up. The deterministic two-stage finalize costs 26 µs at 1 token and 4-15% over default mode from 8 tokens up, in line with the 1.4-14% that [flashinfer#3976](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976) reports.
- **Where the time goes at 512 tokens (default mode, profiled):** The expert GEMMs take 2180 µs in BF16, 1433 µs in MXFP8 and 656 µs in NVFP4, roughly in proportion to weight bytes. MXFP8 is no faster than BF16 overall because its unpermute kernel takes another 842 µs; in batch-invariant mode, MXFP8's expert-order unpermute takes 61 µs, which is why MXFP8 is faster there than in its own default mode.
- **Accuracy:** cosine similarity to vLLM BF16 is about 0.998 for MXFP8 and 0.98 for NVFP4 in both modes, which is the expected precision gap.
- **Memory:** layer memory after the first forward is 18.4 GB for NVFP4 against 14.4 GB for BF16, because the BF16 expert stacks stay resident as the refit source.

**Known gap with EP > 1.** With the NVLS dispatcher, the expert input buffer is sized for the largest batch across all ranks. The vLLM and MXFP8 paths process only the valid rows (vLLM reads a device-side `valid_tokens` count; FlashInfer MXFP8 takes `inference_flashinfer_mxfp8_token_capacity`), but the NVFP4 path quantizes and routes the whole buffer. On Nemotron-3 Super shapes at EP = 4 with an 8192-token buffer, this gives NVFP4 a floor of about 820 µs per layer, against 80 µs for BF16 at 1 token, although NVFP4 is still 1.4x faster than BF16 at 8192 tokens per rank. TODO: bound the NVFP4 rows the same way before marking this PR ready.

Requantizing a layer's expert weights for a refit takes 16.7 ms for 32 Nemotron-3 Super experts.

### Strength: one integration for every NVFP4-weight recipe

FlashInfer's `CuteDslMoEWrapper` runs three NVFP4-weight recipes on the same expert-weight layout: per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 (this PR), per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4, and BF16 x NVFP4. FlashInfer's own tests (`tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py`, cases `w4a4-per-token`, `w4a4-per-tensor`, `w4a16` and `w4a16-relu2`) feed identical weight tensors to all three. Everything this PR builds is therefore shared, and the other two recipes only differ in how activations enter the kernel:
- **Weights:** `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` (BF16 -> packed E2M1 with swizzled E4M3 block scales, padded to 256) and its in-place, CUDA-graph-stable refresh after refit.
- **Kernel plumbing:** the cached wrapper, the two-stage finalize for batch invariance, and writing into the NVLS reduce-scatter buffer.
- **Model integration:** the build, refresh and dispatch in `InferenceGroupedMLP`, and the config validation.
- **Tests:** the BF16 reference, CUDA-graph replay, batch invariance, and the layer and NVLS tests all take the recipe as a parameter.

`inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe` is a recipe choice rather than a bool for this reason: each variant below is a new value, not a new flag.

### How to extend

| | Per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 (this PR) | Per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 | BF16 x NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Config value | `'per_token'` | `'per_tensor'` | `'weight_only'` |
| `quant_mode` | `w4a4` | `w4a4` | `w4a16` |
| FC1 input | `nvfp4_quantize(x, 1/(448*6), per_token_activation=True)` | `nvfp4_quantize(x, a1_scale)` with a fixed scale tensor | BF16 hidden states, padded; not quantized |
| `x_sf` | block scales | block scales | `None` |
| `per_token_scale` | from the quantizer | `None` | `None` |
| `fc1_alpha` / `fc2_alpha` | `1 / w_scale` | `1 / (w_scale * a1_scale)` / `1 / (w_scale * a2_scale)` | `1 / w_scale` |
| `fc2_input_scale` | `1/(448*6)` | `a2_scale` | `None` |
| Use case | RL rollout, no calibration | Serving calibrated (ModelOpt-style) checkpoints | 4x smaller expert weights at BF16 activation accuracy |

`w_scale` is the per-expert weight global scale that `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights` already computes. `a1_scale` / `a2_scale` are the static FC1 / FC2 input scales.

**Per-tensor NVFP4 x NVFP4 (`'per_tensor'`)**
1. **Config:** add `'per_tensor'` to the `Literal`, plus a way to supply the calibrated FC1 and FC2 input scales per layer (from a ModelOpt checkpoint's `input_scale`, or a calibration pass).
2. **`flashinfer_nvfp4.py`:**
   - Make `quant_mode` an argument of `_get_cute_dsl_wrapper` and part of its cache key; it stays `w4a4` here.
   - Add an input path that calls `nvfp4_quantize(padded_hidden, a1_scale)` without `per_token_activation`, and pass `per_token_scale=None`.
   - In `prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights`, fold the activation scales into `fc1_alpha` / `fc2_alpha` and store `a2_scale` in `fc2_input_scale`. The packed weights and block scales don't change.
3. **Graph safety:** keep `a1_scale` / `a2_scale` in fixed device tensors, and confirm the tensor-scale quantizer path triggers no host sync under CUDA graphs.
4. **Tests:** add `'per_tensor'` to the recipe parametrization. The quantizer reference test gains a per-tensor case. The train-gen parity test doesn't apply: TE's per-tensor NVFP4 computes the activation scale from each tensor's amax at runtime, so it has no static-scale counterpart.

**BF16 x NVFP4 (`'weight_only'`)**
1. **Config:** add `'weight_only'` to the `Literal`. No calibration and no new inputs are needed.
2. **`flashinfer_nvfp4.py`:**
   - Create the wrapper with `quant_mode="w4a16"`.
   - Skip activation quantization: pad the BF16 hidden states to `padded_hidden_size` and pass them as `x`, with `x_sf`, `fc2_input_scale` and `per_token_scale` all `None`.
   - Weights, `fc1_alpha`, `fc2_alpha` and the refresh don't change.
3. **Tests:** add `'weight_only'` to the recipe parametrization. The quantizer reference test doesn't apply because there's no activation quantizer. The BF16 reference tolerance can be tighter, since only weights are quantized.

Both variants inherit the rest unchanged: batch invariance through the two-stage finalize (`w4a16` supports it too), CUDA-graph capture, NVLS, refit refresh, and support for squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.

## What is tested

The tests mirror the torch MXFP8 coverage from [#7302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7302) (batch invariance) and [#8195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8195) (train-gen parity) and sit next to those tests. GPU tests skip unless FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 and SM100/SM103 are available; kernel tests are marked `launch_on_gb200`. Results below are from a GB300 4-GPU node (torch 2.11, FlashInfer 0.7.0, TE 2.18).

Run all commands from the repository root. Every NVFP4 kernel, layer, batch-invariance, NVLS and parity test is parametrized over squared-ReLU and SwiGLU.

### 1. Correctness

`tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py`
- **Quantizer bitwise reference** (`test_per_token_nvfp4_quantize_matches_reference`): FlashInfer's per-token quantizer matches a pure-torch reference of the recipe exactly (per-token scales, block-scale bytes and E2M1 codes), including an all-zero row and logspace-spread magnitudes. The reference mirrors TE's NVFP4 quantizer. It runs with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1`; production keeps FlashInfer's default fast math.
- **Gated weight layout** (`test_gated_fc1_is_padded_per_half_and_interleaved_up_gate`, CPU): the SwiGLU FC1 reordering matches FlashInfer's interleaved `[up, gate]` layout exactly, including per-half padding.
- **MoE against BF16** (`test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe_matches_bf16_reference`): the fused MoE stays within the expected NVFP4 error of a BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU MoE (per-token cosine mean > 0.97, minimum > 0.95), including non-256-aligned shapes that exercise padding. Like MXFP8, the MoE itself is checked against BF16, not an emulated reference.
- **Layer level** (`TestNVFP4MoELayer`, NCCL and NVLS dispatchers): an `inference_optimized` MoE layer matches the BF16 training layer; refreshing after a BF16 weight update tracks the update; CUDA-graph replay follows new inputs and refreshed weights.
- **Config, dispatch and refresh plumbing**: accepted and rejected configurations, the missing-capability error message, in-place requantization, and dispatch to the NVFP4 path.

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py
```
Result: 57 passed (squared ReLU and SwiGLU).

### 2. CUDA-graph capture and bitwise replay

`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_inference_kernels.py` (next to `test_mxfp8_swiglu_moe_replays`): `test_per_token_nvfp4_quantize_replays` and `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe_replays`.

`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py`: `TestMoEModules::test_inference_nvfp4_moe_layer_replays` replays the whole MoE layer.

The new kernels are registered in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` as `inference_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe`, and `test_manifest.py` checks the registration.

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_inference_kernels.py -k "nvfp4 or mxfp8"
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py -k nvfp4
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_manifest.py
```
Results: 9 passed (NVFP4 together with the existing MXFP8 cases), 2 passed, 269 passed.

### 3. Batch invariance

- **Kernel** (`test_inference_kernels.py::test_flashinfer_nvfp4_moe_is_batch_invariant`, next to `test_torch_mxfp8_moe_is_batch_invariant`): a target batch gives bitwise identical output alone and inside batches of 193 and 1024 tokens, where the co-batched tokens are 100x larger and routed to the same experts.
- **Local EP** (`test_flashinfer_nvfp4.py::test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_is_batch_invariant`): the same check across local expert offsets, in deterministic and batch-invariant modes.
- **NVLS layer** (`test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py::TestNVLSAllGatherVDispatcher::test_cuda_graph_batch_invariant_nvfp4_moe_layer_uses_ordered_rsv`, next to the MXFP8 equivalent): with EP = 4 the layer writes into the reduce-scatter buffer, reduces with `ordered_reduce_scatter_v`, and CUDA-graph replay equals eager execution bitwise.

These run with the commands in sections 1 and 2, plus:

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py \
  -k "nvfp4 or test_batch_invariant_moe_matches_training"
```

### 4. Train-gen parity (expected failure for now)

`test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py::TestNVLSAllGatherVDispatcher::test_batch_invariant_nvfp4_moe_matches_training`, next to the MXFP8 `test_batch_invariant_moe_matches_training` from #8195. It loads the same weights into a TE training MoE layer running NVFP4 with row-scaled activations (`fp4="e2m1"` with the recipe from the Background section) and into the batch-invariant inference layer, then compares outputs.

**TE does not match bitwise yet.** The test asserts that generation is much closer to TE NVFP4 training than to BF16 (relative error less than half of the error against BF16), then calls `pytest.xfail` when the outputs are not bitwise equal. It measures about 0.03 relative error against TE NVFP4 training versus about 0.20 against BF16 for squared ReLU (maximum absolute difference about 0.0018), and about 0.035 versus 0.23 for SwiGLU (about 0.0008). The test reports XFAIL, which does not fail CI, and will start passing once the kernels are aligned. The known gaps are:
- Training applies the routing probabilities before quantizing the FC2 input; the FlashInfer kernel applies them in the finalize, after FC2.
- The CuTe DSL kernel quantizes the FC2 input inside the FC1 epilogue with approximate reciprocals. `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH` only affects the standalone quantizer, so this step can't be made IEEE-exact today.
- The GEMMs differ in how the FC1 output is rounded and in accumulation order.

Command: the `test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py` command in section 3.

Result: 6 passed, 4 skipped, 2 xfailed (the parity test for squared ReLU and SwiGLU). The skips are pre-existing MXFP8 parity cases that need DeepGEMM BF16 or cuBLASLt 13.5.1.

### 5. Regressions

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_flashinfer_mxfp8.py
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/inference/test_moe_dispatching_and_routing.py
```
Results: 28 passed for `test_flashinfer_mxfp8.py`; 61 passed, 5 skipped and 2 xfailed (the parity test above) for the dispatching file. The skips are pre-existing torch and MXFP8 cases that need DeepGEMM BF16 or cuBLASLt 13.5.1.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

+"""FlashInfer routed-MoE support for per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.
+
+Expert weights are quantized from MCore's BF16 expert stacks with one FP32

+FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX = 448.0

+def require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4() -> None:

+            "inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe."

+def _round_up(value: int, alignment: int) -> int:
+    return (value + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """FC1/FC2 expert stacks in the CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped-GEMM layout.
+
+    Data is packed E2M1 ``[experts, N, K // 2]``. ``*_scale`` is the 6D MMA view
+    of the 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales held in ``*_scale_swizzled``.
+    ``*_alpha`` are the per-expert FP32 dequantization scales and
+    ``fc2_input_scale`` is the per-token recipe constant for the FC2 input.
+    Gated (SwiGLU) FC1 has ``2 * padded_intermediate_size`` rows in FlashInfer's
+    interleaved up/gate order.
+    """
+
+    hidden_size: int
+    intermediate_size: int
+    padded_hidden_size: int
+    padded_intermediate_size: int
+    gated: bool
+    fc1_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_input_scale: torch.Tensor
+
+    @property
+    def num_local_experts(self) -> int:
+        """Number of experts in each stack."""
+        return self.fc1_data.shape[0]
+
+
+def _global_encode_scale(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return the one-element NVFP4 global encode scale for a weight matrix."""
+    amax = weight.abs().amax().float().reshape(1)
+    encode = (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX) / amax
+    return torch.where(amax > 0, encode, torch.ones_like(encode))
+
+
+def _zero_pad(weight: torch.Tensor, padded_rows: int, padded_cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    rows, cols = weight.shape
+    padded = weight.new_zeros(padded_rows, padded_cols, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    padded[:rows, :cols].copy_(weight)
+    return padded
+
+
+def _pad_fc1(weight: torch.Tensor, gated: bool, padded_i: int, padded_h: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Zero-pad one FC1 expert weight into the CuTe DSL row order.
+
+    MCore stores gated FC1 as ``[gate; up]``. FlashInfer expects ``[up; gate]`` with each half
+    padded separately and the halves interleaved in ``_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS``-row blocks.
+    """
+    if not gated:
+        return _zero_pad(weight, padded_i, padded_h)
+    gate, up = weight.chunk(2, dim=0)
+    halves = torch.stack((_zero_pad(up, padded_i, padded_h), _zero_pad(gate, padded_i, padded_h)))
+    blocks = halves.view(2, padded_i // _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, padded_h)
+    return blocks.transpose(0, 1).reshape(2 * padded_i, padded_h)
+
+
+def _quantize_expert(
+    padded: torch.Tensor,
+    data_out: torch.Tensor,
+    swizzled_scale_out: torch.Tensor,
+    alpha_out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Quantize one zero-padded ``[rows, cols]`` expert weight into CuTe DSL NVFP4 storage."""
+    padded_rows, padded_cols = padded.shape
+    encode = _global_encode_scale(padded)
+    data, scale = nvfp4_quantize(padded, encode, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4)
+    data_out.copy_(data.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // 2))
+    swizzled_scale_out.copy_(
+        scale.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    )
+    alpha_out.copy_(encode.reciprocal())
+
+
+def _validate_stacks(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor, fc2_weight: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[int, int, int, bool]:
+    """Return (experts, intermediate, hidden, gated); gated FC1 has twice FC2's input width."""
+    if fc1_weight.ndim != 3 or fc2_weight.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "expected [experts, M, K] expert stacks, got "
+            f"fc1={tuple(fc1_weight.shape)}, fc2={tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}"
+        )
+    experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = fc2_weight.shape
+    fc1_rows = fc1_weight.shape[1]
+    gated = fc1_rows == 2 * intermediate_size
+    if tuple(fc1_weight.shape) != (experts, fc1_rows, hidden_size) or fc1_rows not in (
+        intermediate_size,
+        2 * intermediate_size,
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"FC1 shape {tuple(fc1_weight.shape)} does not match FC2 shape "
+            f"{tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}: expected [experts, intermediate or 2 * intermediate, "
+            "hidden]"
+        )
+    return experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated
+
+
+def _check_refresh_metadata(
+    out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+):
+    expected = (experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated)
+    actual = (
+        out.num_local_experts,
+        out.hidden_size,
+        out.intermediate_size,
+        out.padded_hidden_size,
+        out.padded_intermediate_size,
+        out.gated,
+    )
+    if actual != expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "existing FlashInfer routed NVFP4 weight metadata changed across refit: "
+            f"got {actual}, expected {expected}"
+        )
+

+@torch.no_grad()
+def prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    fc2_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights | None = None,
+) -> FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """Quantize BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU expert stacks into the per-token NVFP4 kernel layout.
+
+    Args:
+        fc1_weight: ``[experts, intermediate, hidden]`` BF16 FC1 weights, or
+            ``[experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden]`` as MCore's ``[gate; up]`` for SwiGLU.
+        fc2_weight: ``[experts, hidden, intermediate]`` BF16 FC2 weights.
+        out: When provided, its tensors are refreshed in place. This preserves
+            addresses captured by CUDA graphs across model refits.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated = _validate_stacks(fc1_weight, fc2_weight)
+    padded_h = _round_up(hidden_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    padded_i = _round_up(intermediate_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    fc1_rows = 2 * padded_i if gated else padded_i
+    device = fc1_weight.device
+
+    if out is None:
+
+        def _empty(*shape, dtype):
+            return torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+        # Each expert's row count is a multiple of 128, so per-expert 128x4-swizzled
+        # scale blocks concatenate into the swizzled layout of the stacked matrix.
+        fc1_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * fc1_rows, padded_h // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        fc2_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * padded_h, padded_i // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        out = FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights(
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            padded_hidden_size=padded_h,
+            padded_intermediate_size=padded_i,
+            gated=gated,
+            fc1_data=_empty(experts, fc1_rows, padded_h // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc1_scale_swizzled=fc1_scale_swizzled,
+            fc1_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc1_scale_swizzled, m=fc1_rows, k=padded_h, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc1_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_data=_empty(experts, padded_h, padded_i // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc2_scale_swizzled=fc2_scale_swizzled,
+            fc2_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc2_scale_swizzled, m=padded_h, k=padded_i, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc2_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_input_scale=torch.full(
+                (1,), PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            ),
+        )
+    else:
+        _check_refresh_metadata(
+            out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+        )
+
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _pad_fc1(fc1_weight[expert], gated, padded_i, padded_h),
+            out.fc1_data[expert],
+            out.fc1_scale_swizzled[expert * fc1_rows : (expert + 1) * fc1_rows],
+            out.fc1_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _zero_pad(fc2_weight[expert], padded_h, padded_i),
+            out.fc2_data[expert],
+            out.fc2_scale_swizzled[expert * padded_h : (expert + 1) * padded_h],
+            out.fc2_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+    for swizzled, mma, m, k in (
+        (out.fc1_scale_swizzled, out.fc1_scale, fc1_rows, padded_h),
+        (out.fc2_scale_swizzled, out.fc2_scale, padded_h, padded_i),
+    ):
+        converted = convert_sf_to_mma_layout(swizzled, m=m, k=k, num_groups=experts)
+        if converted.data_ptr() != mma.data_ptr():
+            mma.copy_(converted)
+    return out

+def quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor, padded_hidden_size: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pad and quantize routed-MoE input with one FP32 scale per token.
+
+    Returns packed E2M1 data ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 2]``, linear block scales
+    ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 16]`` (as returned by FlashInfer), and FP32
+    per-token scales ``[tokens]``.
+    """
+    hidden_padding = padded_hidden_size - hidden_states.shape[-1]
+    if hidden_padding < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"padded hidden size {padded_hidden_size} is smaller than input hidden size "
+            f"{hidden_states.shape[-1]}"
+        )
+    padded_hidden = F.pad(hidden_states, (0, hidden_padding)) if hidden_padding else hidden_states
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = nvfp4_quantize(
+        padded_hidden.contiguous(),
+        PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE,
+        sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear,
+        per_token_activation=True,
+    )
+    hidden_scale = hidden_scale.reshape(
+        hidden_states.shape[0], padded_hidden_size // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    return quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale
+

+def _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    num_experts: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    device: torch.device,
+):
+    # The fused finalize accumulates top-k routes with output-dtype atomics, whose
+    # order is not fixed; the two-stage finalize reduces each token's routes in order.
+    use_fused_finalize = not (
+        torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled() or is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+    )
+    key = (
+        use_fused_finalize,
+        num_experts,
+        top_k,
+        weights.padded_hidden_size,
+        weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+        weights.num_local_experts,
+        local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type,
+        str(device),
+    )
+    wrapper = _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS.get(key)
+    if wrapper is None:
+        # Persistent stream/event resources are created here, outside graph capture.
+        wrapper = CuteDslMoEWrapper(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            hidden_size=weights.padded_hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+            use_cuda_graph=True,
+            num_local_experts=weights.num_local_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            output_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=str(device),
+            activation_type=activation_type,
+            use_fused_finalize=use_fused_finalize,
+            quant_mode="w4a4",
+        )
+        _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS[key] = wrapper
+    return wrapper
+

+            )

+    return output

+def _reference_moe(hidden, fc1, fc2, topk_ids, topk_weights):
+    """BF16 squared-ReLU MoE, or SwiGLU when FC1 holds MCore's [gate; up] halves."""
+    gated = fc1.shape[1] == 2 * fc2.shape[2]
+    output = torch.zeros_like(hidden, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for slot in range(topk_ids.shape[1]):
+        for expert in range(fc1.shape[0]):
+            rows = topk_ids[:, slot] == expert
+            if not rows.any():
+                continue
+            fc1_out = hidden[rows].float() @ fc1[expert].float().t()
+            if gated:
+                gate, up = fc1_out.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+                intermediate = F.silu(gate) * up
+            else:
+                intermediate = F.relu(fc1_out).square()
+            expert_out = intermediate @ fc2[expert].float().t()
+            output[rows] += topk_weights[rows, slot : slot + 1] * expert_out
+    return output

+def _assert_close_to_reference(output, reference):
+    # Exact NVFP4 emulation of these shapes gives per-token cosine ~0.98 mean and ~0.965 at

+# E2M1 code -> value; bit 3 is the sign.
+_E2M1_MAGNITUDES = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+_E2M1_VALUES = _E2M1_MAGNITUDES + tuple(-value for value in _E2M1_MAGNITUDES)
+# (upper bound, bound inclusive, value): round-half-to-even onto the E2M1 grid.
+_E2M1_ROUNDING = (
+    (0.25, True, 0.0),
+    (0.75, False, 0.5),
+    (1.25, True, 1.0),
+    (1.75, False, 1.5),
+    (2.5, True, 2.0),
+    (3.5, False, 3.0),
+    (5.0, True, 4.0),
+)
+
+
+def _ref_round_to_e2m1(x):
+    magnitude = x.abs()
+    out = torch.full_like(magnitude, 6.0)
+    for bound, inclusive, value in reversed(_E2M1_ROUNDING):
+        below = magnitude <= bound if inclusive else magnitude < bound
+        out = torch.where(below, torch.full_like(out, value), out)
+    return out * torch.sign(x)
+

+def _ref_per_token_nvfp4_quantize(x):
+    """Pure-PyTorch per-token NVFP4 quantizer mirroring Transformer Engine's reference.
+
+    Returns E2M1 values ``[rows, cols]`` (FP32), E4M3 block decode scales
+    ``[rows, cols // 16]`` and the FP32 per-token decode scales ``[rows]``.
+    """
+    rows, cols = x.shape
+    blocks = x.float().view(rows, cols // 16, 16)
+    block_amax = blocks.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    row_amax = block_amax.amax(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+
+    # Tensor-by-tensor division: a Python scalar numerator becomes reciprocal-then-multiply.
+    def const(value):
+        return torch.tensor(value, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+
+    fp32_max = const(torch.finfo(torch.float32).max)
+    global_encode = torch.minimum(torch.div(const(448.0 * 6.0), row_amax), fp32_max)
+    global_encode = torch.where(global_encode == 0, torch.ones_like(global_encode), global_encode)
+    global_decode = torch.div(const(1.0), global_encode)
+    decode = torch.minimum(block_amax * (global_encode * torch.reciprocal(const(6.0))), fp32_max)
+    decode = decode.clamp(-448.0, 448.0).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    encode = torch.minimum(torch.div(const(1.0), decode.float() * global_decode), fp32_max)
+    values = _ref_round_to_e2m1((blocks * encode).clamp(-6.0, 6.0)).reshape(rows, cols)
+    # An all-zero row reports a zero per-token scale.
+    per_token_decode = torch.where(row_amax == 0, torch.zeros_like(global_decode), global_decode)
+    return values, decode.squeeze(-1), per_token_decode.reshape(-1)
+
+
+def _unpack_e2m1(packed):
+    """Decode packed E2M1 bytes ``[rows, cols // 2]``; the low nibble is the even element."""
+    lookup = torch.tensor(_E2M1_VALUES, device=packed.device)
+    packed = packed.view(torch.uint8).long()
+    return torch.stack((lookup[packed & 0xF], lookup[packed >> 4]), dim=-1).flatten(-2)

+    )
+    key = (
+        use_fused_finalize,
+        num_experts,
+        top_k,
+        weights.padded_hidden_size,
+        weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+        weights.num_local_experts,
+        local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type,
+        str(device),
+    )

+        wrapper = CuteDslMoEWrapper(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            hidden_size=weights.padded_hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+            use_cuda_graph=True,
+            num_local_experts=weights.num_local_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            output_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=str(device),
+            activation_type=activation_type,
+            use_fused_finalize=use_fused_finalize,
+            quant_mode="w4a4",
+        )

+    return wrapper

+
+def flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe(

+    num_experts: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:

+

+        device=quantized_hidden.device,
+    )
+    output = wrapper.run(

+        weights.fc1_alpha,

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""FlashInfer routed-MoE support for per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.
+
+Expert weights are quantized from MCore's BF16 expert stacks with one FP32
+global scale per expert. Activations are quantized online with one FP32 scale
+per token, so no calibration or static input scale is required. The experts
+run on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.custom_layers.batch_invariant_kernels import (
+    is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled,
+)
+
+try:
+    import flashinfer
+    from flashinfer import ActivationType, SfLayout, nvfp4_quantize
+    from packaging.version import Version
+
+    # Per-token NVFP4 Relu2 MoE landed in FlashInfer 0.7.0 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3645).
+    if Version(flashinfer.__version__).release < (0, 7, 0):
+        raise ImportError(
+            f"FlashInfer {flashinfer.__version__} lacks the per-token NVFP4 Relu2 MoE kernels"
+        )
+    from flashinfer import CuteDslMoEWrapper
+    from flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils import convert_sf_to_mma_layout
+
+    _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR: ImportError | None = None
+except ImportError as exc:
+    _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR = exc
+
+HAVE_FLASHINFER_ROUTED_NVFP4 = _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR is None
+
+NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX = 6.0
+FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX = 448.0
+# Per-token quantization folds the row amax into the per-token scale, so the base
+# global scale is the recipe constant 1 / (E4M3_MAX * E2M1_MAX). FlashInfer rejects
+# other values. It must be a Python float: a tensor triggers a host sync.
+PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE = 1.0 / (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX)
+# GEMM K/N padding: the CuTe DSL grouped GEMMs need N % 128 and full 256-wide FP4 K tiles.
+_ALIGNMENT = 256
+# Gated FC1 rows are [up, gate] blocks of this many rows each, alternating.
+_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS = 64
+
+_CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS: dict = {}
+
+
+def require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4() -> None:
+    """Raise an error when the per-token NVFP4 routed-MoE APIs are unavailable."""
+    if not HAVE_FLASHINFER_ROUTED_NVFP4:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "FlashInfer per-token NVFP4 MoE requires FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 with "
+            "nvidia-cutlass-dsl. Upgrade flashinfer-python or disable "
+            "inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe."
+        ) from _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR
+
+
+def _round_up(value: int, alignment: int) -> int:
+    return (value + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """FC1/FC2 expert stacks in the CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped-GEMM layout.
+
+    Data is packed E2M1 ``[experts, N, K // 2]``. ``*_scale`` is the 6D MMA view
+    of the 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales held in ``*_scale_swizzled``.
+    ``*_alpha`` are the per-expert FP32 dequantization scales and
+    ``fc2_input_scale`` is the per-token recipe constant for the FC2 input.
+    Gated (SwiGLU) FC1 has ``2 * padded_intermediate_size`` rows in FlashInfer's
+    interleaved up/gate order.
+    """
+
+    hidden_size: int
+    intermediate_size: int
+    padded_hidden_size: int
+    padded_intermediate_size: int
+    gated: bool
+    fc1_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_input_scale: torch.Tensor
+
+    @property
+    def num_local_experts(self) -> int:
+        """Number of experts in each stack."""
+        return self.fc1_data.shape[0]
+
+
+def _global_encode_scale(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return the one-element NVFP4 global encode scale for a weight matrix."""
+    amax = weight.abs().amax().float().reshape(1)
+    encode = (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX) / amax
+    return torch.where(amax > 0, encode, torch.ones_like(encode))
+
+
+def _zero_pad(weight: torch.Tensor, padded_rows: int, padded_cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    rows, cols = weight.shape
+    padded = weight.new_zeros(padded_rows, padded_cols, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    padded[:rows, :cols].copy_(weight)
+    return padded
+
+
+def _pad_fc1(weight: torch.Tensor, gated: bool, padded_i: int, padded_h: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Zero-pad one FC1 expert weight into the CuTe DSL row order.
+
+    MCore stores gated FC1 as ``[gate; up]``. FlashInfer expects ``[up; gate]`` with each half
+    padded separately and the halves interleaved in ``_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS``-row blocks.
+    """
+    if not gated:
+        return _zero_pad(weight, padded_i, padded_h)
+    gate, up = weight.chunk(2, dim=0)
+    halves = torch.stack((_zero_pad(up, padded_i, padded_h), _zero_pad(gate, padded_i, padded_h)))
+    blocks = halves.view(2, padded_i // _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, padded_h)
+    return blocks.transpose(0, 1).reshape(2 * padded_i, padded_h)
+
+
+def _quantize_expert(
+    padded: torch.Tensor,
+    data_out: torch.Tensor,
+    swizzled_scale_out: torch.Tensor,
+    alpha_out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Quantize one zero-padded ``[rows, cols]`` expert weight into CuTe DSL NVFP4 storage."""
+    padded_rows, padded_cols = padded.shape
+    encode = _global_encode_scale(padded)
+    data, scale = nvfp4_quantize(padded, encode, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4)
+    data_out.copy_(data.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // 2))
+    swizzled_scale_out.copy_(
+        scale.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    )
+    alpha_out.copy_(encode.reciprocal())
+
+
+def _validate_stacks(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor, fc2_weight: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[int, int, int, bool]:
+    """Return (experts, intermediate, hidden, gated); gated FC1 has twice FC2's input width."""
+    if fc1_weight.ndim != 3 or fc2_weight.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "expected [experts, M, K] expert stacks, got "
+            f"fc1={tuple(fc1_weight.shape)}, fc2={tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}"
+        )
+    experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = fc2_weight.shape
+    fc1_rows = fc1_weight.shape[1]
+    gated = fc1_rows == 2 * intermediate_size
+    if tuple(fc1_weight.shape) != (experts, fc1_rows, hidden_size) or fc1_rows not in (
+        intermediate_size,
+        2 * intermediate_size,
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"FC1 shape {tuple(fc1_weight.shape)} does not match FC2 shape "
+            f"{tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}: expected [experts, intermediate or 2 * intermediate, "
+            "hidden]"
+        )
+    return experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated
+
+
+def _check_refresh_metadata(
+    out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+):
+    expected = (experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated)
+    actual = (
+        out.num_local_experts,
+        out.hidden_size,
+        out.intermediate_size,
+        out.padded_hidden_size,
+        out.padded_intermediate_size,
+        out.gated,
+    )
+    if actual != expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "existing FlashInfer routed NVFP4 weight metadata changed across refit: "
+            f"got {actual}, expected {expected}"
+        )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    fc2_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights | None = None,
+) -> FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """Quantize BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU expert stacks into the per-token NVFP4 kernel layout.
+
+    Args:
+        fc1_weight: ``[experts, intermediate, hidden]`` BF16 FC1 weights, or
+            ``[experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden]`` as MCore's ``[gate; up]`` for SwiGLU.
+        fc2_weight: ``[experts, hidden, intermediate]`` BF16 FC2 weights.
+        out: When provided, its tensors are refreshed in place. This preserves
+            addresses captured by CUDA graphs across model refits.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated = _validate_stacks(fc1_weight, fc2_weight)
+    padded_h = _round_up(hidden_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    padded_i = _round_up(intermediate_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    fc1_rows = 2 * padded_i if gated else padded_i
+    device = fc1_weight.device
+
+    if out is None:
+
+        def _empty(*shape, dtype):
+            return torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+        # Each expert's row count is a multiple of 128, so per-expert 128x4-swizzled
+        # scale blocks concatenate into the swizzled layout of the stacked matrix.
+        fc1_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * fc1_rows, padded_h // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        fc2_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * padded_h, padded_i // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        out = FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights(
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            padded_hidden_size=padded_h,
+            padded_intermediate_size=padded_i,
+            gated=gated,
+            fc1_data=_empty(experts, fc1_rows, padded_h // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc1_scale_swizzled=fc1_scale_swizzled,
+            fc1_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc1_scale_swizzled, m=fc1_rows, k=padded_h, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc1_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_data=_empty(experts, padded_h, padded_i // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc2_scale_swizzled=fc2_scale_swizzled,
+            fc2_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc2_scale_swizzled, m=padded_h, k=padded_i, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc2_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_input_scale=torch.full(
+                (1,), PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            ),
+        )
+    else:
+        _check_refresh_metadata(
+            out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+        )
+
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _pad_fc1(fc1_weight[expert], gated, padded_i, padded_h),
+            out.fc1_data[expert],
+            out.fc1_scale_swizzled[expert * fc1_rows : (expert + 1) * fc1_rows],
+            out.fc1_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _zero_pad(fc2_weight[expert], padded_h, padded_i),
+            out.fc2_data[expert],
+            out.fc2_scale_swizzled[expert * padded_h : (expert + 1) * padded_h],
+            out.fc2_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+    for swizzled, mma, m, k in (
+        (out.fc1_scale_swizzled, out.fc1_scale, fc1_rows, padded_h),
+        (out.fc2_scale_swizzled, out.fc2_scale, padded_h, padded_i),
+    ):
+        converted = convert_sf_to_mma_layout(swizzled, m=m, k=k, num_groups=experts)
+        if converted.data_ptr() != mma.data_ptr():
+            mma.copy_(converted)
+    return out
+
+
+def quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor, padded_hidden_size: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pad and quantize routed-MoE input with one FP32 scale per token.
+
+    Returns packed E2M1 data ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 2]``, linear block scales
+    ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 16]`` (as returned by FlashInfer), and FP32
+    per-token scales ``[tokens]``.
+    """
+    hidden_padding = padded_hidden_size - hidden_states.shape[-1]
+    if hidden_padding < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"padded hidden size {padded_hidden_size} is smaller than input hidden size "
+            f"{hidden_states.shape[-1]}"
+        )
+    padded_hidden = F.pad(hidden_states, (0, hidden_padding)) if hidden_padding else hidden_states
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = nvfp4_quantize(
+        padded_hidden.contiguous(),
+        PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE,
+        sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear,
+        per_token_activation=True,
+    )
+    hidden_scale = hidden_scale.reshape(
+        hidden_states.shape[0], padded_hidden_size // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    return quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale
+
+
+def _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    num_experts: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    device: torch.device,
+):
+    # The fused finalize accumulates top-k routes with output-dtype atomics, whose
+    # order is not fixed; the two-stage finalize reduces each token's routes in order.
+    use_fused_finalize = not (
+        torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled() or is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+    )
+    key = (
+        use_fused_finalize,
+        num_experts,
+        top_k,
+        weights.padded_hidden_size,
+        weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+        weights.num_local_experts,
+        local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type,
+        str(device),
+    )
+    wrapper = _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS.get(key)
+    if wrapper is None:
+        # Persistent stream/event resources are created here, outside graph capture.
+        wrapper = CuteDslMoEWrapper(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            hidden_size=weights.padded_hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+            use_cuda_graph=True,
+            num_local_experts=weights.num_local_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            output_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=str(device),
+            activation_type=activation_type,
+            use_fused_finalize=use_fused_finalize,
+            quant_mode="w4a4",
+        )
+        _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS[key] = wrapper
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    routing_map: torch.Tensor,
+    probabilities: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    *,
+    num_experts: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Run the FlashInfer per-token NVFP4 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU MoE.
+
+    Rows whose routing entries are -1 contribute zero output, so a graph-stable
+    dispatcher buffer may be passed in full.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    expected_activation = ActivationType.Swiglu if weights.gated else ActivationType.Relu2
+    if activation_type != expected_activation.value:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{'Gated' if weights.gated else 'Non-gated'} per-token NVFP4 expert weights need "
+            f"activation_type={expected_activation.name}; got activation_type={activation_type}"
+        )
+    if hidden_states.shape[-1] != weights.hidden_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"hidden size {hidden_states.shape[-1]} does not match expert hidden size "
+            f"{weights.hidden_size}"
+        )
+    if probabilities.dtype != torch.float32:
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"FlashInfer routed MoE requires FP32 probabilities; got {probabilities.dtype}"
+        )
+
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+        hidden_states, weights.padded_hidden_size
+    )
+    wrapper = _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+        weights,
+        num_experts=num_experts,
+        top_k=routing_map.shape[1],
+        local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type=activation_type,
+        device=quantized_hidden.device,
+    )
+    output = wrapper.run(
+        quantized_hidden,
+        hidden_scale.unsqueeze(-1),
+        routing_map.to(torch.int32),
+        probabilities,
+        weights.fc1_data,
+        weights.fc1_scale,
+        weights.fc1_alpha,
+        weights.fc2_input_scale,
+        weights.fc2_data,
+        weights.fc2_scale,
+        weights.fc2_alpha,
+        per_token_scale=per_token_scale,
+    )[:, : weights.hidden_size]
